name: Wagner k-tree / generalized birthday (k-XOR, k-SUM) and Schroeppel-Shamir / Dinur-Dunkelman-Keller-Shamir dissection
description: Wagner (CRYPTO 2002) solves the k-list generalized birthday problem (find one element per list with XOR/sum equal to target) in time and memory about 2^{n/(1+floor(log2 k))} for n-bit values by merging lists pairwise in a tree while zeroing a slice of bits per level, given lists of size 2^{n/(1+log k)}. Schroeppel-Shamir (1979/81) gives 2^{n/2} time with 2^{n/4} space for 4-list/Subset Sum; Dinur-Dunkelman-Keller-Shamir dissection (CRYPTO 2012) generalizes this to k-list problems with reduced memory, and later work (Dinur 2020 time-memory curve; Esser-May; Nikolic-Sasaki; Naya-Plasencia-Schrottenloher) refines trade-offs. These are algorithms that FIND a solution to a single (planted/expected-count) relation; they do not count or bound the number of equal-sum subset pairs. For this repo they are the cost model for locating the relations C1 counts: if N_c large implies many equal-sum disjoint pairs, a collision-finding algorithm in time ~ 2^{n/2} (MITM) or less when relations are abundant could exploit them.

status_and_verification: Peer-reviewed (all). NOT checked against primary text: only web-search summaries (search results for Wagner K-tree complexity N^{1/(floor(log K)+1)} and dissection memory improvements) were read. Exact statements below are from standard knowledge plus those snippets. [uncertain]
key_theorem_or_bound: Wagner K-tree: for K=2^t lists of size ~2^{n/(t+1)} of n-bit values, find a K-tuple with XOR 0 in time/memory O~(2^{n/(1+log K)}) (rounded down to floor(log K)). Schroeppel-Shamir: Subset Sum / 4-list problem in O~(2^{n/2}) time, O~(2^{n/4}) space. Dissection (DDKS12): k-list problems with total list size N=2^{n/k}-type input solved in time ~N^{ceil(sqrt(2k)...)} -type exponents with memory below N^{k/2}; exact formula not verified. [uncertain]
regime_exponents: For Subset Sum with n inputs and exponent-size targets, view as k-SUM on n/k-size groups: Wagner needs lists of size 2^{n/k} and an expected-solution count of >=1 after each merge level; the baseline is MITM 2^{n/2}. Wagner only beats 2^{n/2} when many solutions exist (e.g. density > 1 / PESS-like regime), otherwise lists would be needed larger than 2^{n/k}. None of the thresholds 0.311n / 0.661n are addressed by these papers. [uncertain]
proof_type_and_tools: Combinatorial / probabilistic (random-list model, birthday collision counting; independence of lists after partial merges). Dissection uses combinatorial list splitting with partial-sum enumeration.
quantitative_loss: Wagner requires independence/uniformity of list elements; analysis is expectation-based (no exponential loss under random model, but guarantees fail for adversarial inputs, where structured instances can break the merge-level uniformity). No BSG/PFR style loss; the dependence is on solution-count assumptions.
worst_case_vs_average_case: Average-case / random-oracle model (lists uniform). Does not transfer to worst case in general; worst-case subset-sum variants need hashing + representation technique (Howgrave-Graham-Joux), which in the worst case is only known for Equal-Subset-Sum type problems.
coefficient_set: Natively XOR over F_2^n or sums mod 2^n with one element per list; Subset Sum coefficient set {0,1} is encoded by making each list the two-element set {0,x_i}-sums of a block. Signed {-1,0,1} versions correspond to lists {-x,0,x} (3^{n/k} sized blocks).
subset_size_regime: k-tuple with one element per list (fixed k lists); the Subset Sum embedding covers all subsets, not Theta(n)-subsets specifically. Cardinality constraints require extra weight-restricted list handling.
relevance_to_Nc: Gives the algorithmic cost of EXTRACTING equal-sum pairs: if N_c (number of equal-sum disjoint pairs of Theta(n)-subsets) is exponentially large, a Wagner-type search with that many relations needs lists shorter than 2^{n/2}, which is the mechanism by which a lower bound on N_c would convert into an algorithm. Conversely a Wagner-style upper bound on cost-per-relation gives a budget N_c * cost vs 2^{n/2}. Does not itself bound N_c.
relevance_to_Dstar: Indirect: D* small means few distinct balanced half-sums, i.e. heavy collisions among half-subset sums, which is the regime where list sizes shrink and Wagner/dissection-type merging is effective. No result bounds D*.
applicability_gap: Needs independent uniform lists; adversarial integers break it. Counts of solutions are assumed, not proved. Single-target search rather than counting all pairs; {0,1} Theta(n)-subset constraint and disjointness not handled; time exponent 1/(1+log k) assumes k=2^t and large modulus 2^n.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Instances with all subset sums distinct (e.g. Sidon-like / superincreasing-ish or random with 2^{Omega(n)} bit lengths) have few or no equal-sum pairs so Wagner gives nothing; for such inputs the 2^{n/2} MITM bound is the best known. Rank-d GAP generators give many collisions (N_c large).
dependency_chain: Composes with the representation technique (HGJ), Schroeppel-Shamir for space, and OV reduction (Nederlof-Wegrzycki) to form branch-or-bin: if collisions abound, find them cheaply; otherwise structure (large bins) is absent and MITM is needed.
constructiveness: Fully algorithmic; time 2^{n/(1+log k)} (Wagner), memory similar; dissection reduces memory at higher time.
lean_formalizable: Unlikely to be worthwhile: probabilistic list-model arguments; only counting statements (pigeonhole on partial sums) are mathlib-free formalizable.
computational_check: Not assessed from source (cryptanalytic scale, e.g. n up to ~100+ bits). At n<=40 the repo scripts could directly enumerate all 2^n subset sums and count equal-sum pairs, so Wagner is unnecessary for checking C1. [uncertain]
next_experiment: Write a script that, for generated instances (random, Sidon-like, rank-d GAP) with n<=40, counts N_c exactly and compares to the expected number of relations a Wagner k=4 / k=8 pipeline would need to hit 2^{n/2}.
open_issues: Time-memory tradeoff for large k is still being improved (Dinur 2020 and later). No worst-case guarantee; does not address Theta(n) subset-size restriction; primary text not read in this pass.
